questions.question: A global enterprise with 500+ AWS accounts across multiple business units needs to implement a centralized security and compliance framework. The organization requires different security controls for development, staging, and production environments, with some business units having stricter regulatory requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS). The solution must support automated account provisioning, centralized logging, and cross-account resource sharing while maintaining cost allocation visibility. Which combination of services and architectural patterns would BEST address these requirements?
options: Use AWS Control Tower with custom OUs for each compliance requirement, implement Service Control Policies (SCPs) at the OU level, deploy AWS Config rules organization-wide, and use AWS Cost and Billing Console with detailed tagging strategy
Deploy AWS Organizations with a flat account structure, use IAM policies for access control, implement AWS CloudTrail in each account, and use AWS Budgets for cost management

Use AWS Control Tower with a multi-level OU structure (Security, Compliance, Business Units), implement SCPs and Resource Control Policies (RCPs), deploy AWS Security Hub with delegated administrator, use AWS Cost Categories with allocation tags, and implement AWS RAM for resource sharing
Create separate AWS Organizations for each business unit, use cross-organization trust relationships, implement AWS SSO federation, and use consolidated billing
questions.explanation: Option C provides the most comprehensive solution: AWS Control Tower with multi-level OUs allows granular organization, SCPs and RCPs provide layered security controls, Security Hub with delegated administrator enables centralized security monitoring, Cost Categories with allocation tags provide detailed cost visibility, and AWS RAM enables secure cross-account resource sharing. This architecture supports all requirements including automated provisioning, centralized logging, and regulatory compliance.

questions.question: A financial services company is designing a new microservices-based trading platform that must process 100,000 transactions per second with sub-millisecond latency requirements. The system needs to maintain ACID compliance, support real-time analytics, and provide disaster recovery across multiple regions. Data must be encrypted at rest and in transit, with audit trails for all transactions. Which architecture would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Use Amazon ECS with Fargate, Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ, Amazon ElastiCache for Redis, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for analytics
Deploy Amazon EKS with EC2 instances, Amazon DynamoDB with Global Tables, Amazon MemoryDB for Redis, Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose, and AWS X-Ray for tracing
Use AWS Lambda with Amazon API Gateway, Amazon Aurora Global Database, Amazon ElastiCache for Redis Cluster Mode, Amazon Kinesis Analytics, and AWS CloudTrail
Deploy Amazon ECS on EC2 with placement groups, Amazon DynamoDB with DAX, Amazon MSK, Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics, and AWS Config for compliance
questions.explanation: Option B best addresses the high-performance requirements: EKS with EC2 instances provides the control and performance needed for sub-millisecond latency, DynamoDB with Global Tables offers single-digit millisecond performance with multi-region replication, MemoryDB for Redis provides in-memory performance with ACID compliance, Kinesis Data Firehose handles real-time analytics, and X-Ray provides distributed tracing for microservices monitoring.

questions.question: An e-commerce platform running on AWS is experiencing performance degradation during peak shopping periods. The current architecture uses Application Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Groups with EC2 instances, RDS MySQL with read replicas, and ElastiCache. CloudWatch metrics show high CPU utilization on database instances, increased response times, and occasional 5xx errors. The company wants to optimize performance while minimizing costs and maintaining data consistency. Which combination of improvements would provide the MOST effective optimization?
options: Migrate to Aurora Serverless v2, implement Aurora Global Database, add more read replicas, and increase ElastiCache cluster size

Implement database connection pooling with RDS Proxy, migrate to Aurora MySQL with Aurora Replicas, add CloudFront CDN, implement application-level caching, and use Spot Instances in Auto Scaling Groups
Scale up RDS instance types, add more read replicas across multiple AZs, implement Redis Cluster mode, and use Dedicated Hosts for predictable performance
Migrate to DynamoDB with DAX, implement API Gateway with caching, use Lambda for compute, and add CloudFront with custom origins
questions.explanation: Option B provides comprehensive optimization: RDS Proxy reduces connection overhead and improves database efficiency, Aurora MySQL offers better performance and scaling than RDS MySQL, CloudFront reduces load on origin servers, application-level caching reduces database queries, and Spot Instances provide cost optimization while maintaining performance during peak periods.

questions.question: A manufacturing company needs to migrate 200 on-premises servers running legacy applications to AWS within 6 months. The applications have complex interdependencies, use proprietary databases, and require minimal downtime during migration. Some applications are suitable for containerization, while others need to remain on virtual machines. The company wants to modernize where possible while ensuring business continuity. Which migration strategy would be MOST appropriate?
options: Use AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) for all servers, perform lift-and-shift migration, then modernize applications post-migration

Implement a phased approach using AWS Migration Hub for orchestration, use MGN for legacy applications, AWS App2Container for containerizable applications, and AWS Database Migration Service for database migrations
Use AWS Server Migration Service (SMS) for all virtual machines, AWS DataSync for data migration, and manual application reconfiguration
Migrate all applications to AWS Lambda using the Serverless Application Model (SAM), with Amazon RDS for databases
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive and appropriate migration strategy: Migration Hub provides centralized orchestration and tracking, MGN handles complex legacy applications with minimal downtime, App2Container modernizes suitable applications to containers, and DMS handles database migrations with minimal downtime. This phased approach balances modernization with business continuity requirements.

questions.question: A healthcare organization with multiple subsidiaries needs to implement a multi-account AWS environment that complies with HIPAA requirements. Each subsidiary must have isolated environments for development, staging, and production, with centralized security monitoring and audit logging. The solution must support federated access from the organization's Active Directory and provide granular cost allocation. Which architectural approach would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Create separate AWS Organizations for each subsidiary, implement AWS SSO with AD Connector, use CloudTrail in each account, and AWS Cost Explorer for cost analysis

Use AWS Control Tower with OU structure (Root > Subsidiaries > Environment), implement AWS SSO with AD integration, deploy Security Hub with delegated administrator, use organization-wide CloudTrail, and implement detailed tagging for cost allocation
Deploy AWS Organizations with flat account structure, use IAM roles for cross-account access, implement GuardDuty in each account, and use AWS Budgets for cost management
Use AWS Control Tower with basic OU structure, implement AWS Directory Service, deploy Config rules manually, and use Cost and Billing Console
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive HIPAA-compliant solution: Control Tower with hierarchical OU structure enables proper isolation and governance, AWS SSO with AD integration provides federated access, Security Hub with delegated administrator enables centralized security monitoring, organization-wide CloudTrail ensures comprehensive audit logging, and detailed tagging enables granular cost allocation across subsidiaries and environments.

questions.question: A media streaming company is designing a new global content delivery platform that must support 10 million concurrent users across 6 continents. The platform requires adaptive bitrate streaming, real-time analytics, content personalization, and must comply with data residency requirements in different regions. The solution must automatically scale based on demand and optimize costs during low-usage periods. Which architecture would BEST address these requirements?
options: Use CloudFront with multiple origins, EC2 Auto Scaling Groups in each region, RDS with cross-region read replicas, and Kinesis Data Streams for analytics

Deploy CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for personalization, use MediaLive and MediaPackage for streaming, implement DynamoDB Global Tables for user data, Kinesis Data Analytics for real-time insights, and S3 with Cross-Region Replication for content storage
Use API Gateway with regional endpoints, ECS Fargate for compute, Aurora Global Database, ElastiCache Global Datastore, and CloudWatch for monitoring
Implement Application Load Balancer with Global Accelerator, EKS clusters in each region, DocumentDB with cross-region replication, and MSK for streaming analytics
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive media streaming solution: CloudFront with Lambda@Edge enables global content delivery with edge personalization, MediaLive and MediaPackage are purpose-built for adaptive bitrate streaming, DynamoDB Global Tables provide low-latency user data access globally while supporting data residency, Kinesis Data Analytics enables real-time analytics, and S3 with CRR ensures content availability across regions.

questions.question: A SaaS company's application is experiencing intermittent performance issues and increased costs. The current architecture uses ALB, ECS tasks, RDS PostgreSQL, and ElastiCache. CloudWatch shows high memory utilization on ECS tasks, database connection pool exhaustion, and cache miss rates above 40%. The company wants to improve performance and reduce costs without major architectural changes. Which optimization strategy would be MOST effective?
options: Increase ECS task memory allocation, scale up RDS instance, and add more ElastiCache nodes

Implement ECS Service Auto Scaling based on memory utilization, deploy RDS Proxy for connection pooling, optimize cache TTL settings and implement cache warming strategies, and use Spot capacity for non-critical ECS tasks
Migrate to Fargate Spot, use Aurora Serverless, and implement Redis Cluster mode
Add more ECS tasks, implement read replicas, and increase ElastiCache memory
questions.explanation: Option B provides targeted optimizations addressing root causes: ECS Service Auto Scaling based on memory utilization provides dynamic scaling, RDS Proxy solves connection pool exhaustion, optimized cache strategies reduce miss rates, and Spot capacity reduces costs. This approach improves performance while optimizing costs without requiring major architectural changes.

questions.question: A financial institution is migrating a critical trading system from on-premises to AWS. The system processes millions of transactions daily, requires sub-second latency, and must maintain 99.99% availability. The current system uses Oracle RAC, IBM MQ, and custom C++ applications. Regulatory requirements mandate data encryption, audit trails, and the ability to replay transactions. The migration must be completed with zero data loss and minimal downtime. Which migration approach would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Use AWS DMS for Oracle to RDS migration, replace IBM MQ with Amazon MQ, containerize C++ applications with ECS, and implement blue-green deployment

Migrate Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL using DMS with ongoing replication, replace IBM MQ with Amazon MSK, modernize applications to microservices on EKS, implement AWS X-Ray for tracing, and use AWS Backup for point-in-time recovery

Keep Oracle on EC2 with RAC, use Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ, containerize applications with ECS on EC2, implement Multi-AZ deployment, use EBS encryption, CloudTrail for auditing, and DMS for ongoing replication during cutover
Migrate to DynamoDB with DAX, use EventBridge for messaging, convert to Lambda functions, and implement DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery
questions.explanation: Option C provides the safest migration path for a critical trading system: Keeping Oracle RAC on EC2 maintains performance and compatibility, Amazon MQ provides managed messaging with minimal changes, containerized applications enable better resource utilization, Multi-AZ ensures high availability, EBS encryption and CloudTrail meet regulatory requirements, and DMS enables zero-downtime cutover with ongoing replication.

questions.question: A company with 50 AWS accounts wants to centrally manage security policies and ensure all accounts comply with corporate standards. They need to prevent the creation of public S3 buckets and restrict EC2 instance types to approved families. Which AWS service would be MOST appropriate for implementing these requirements?
options: AWS Config with organization-wide rules
AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs)
AWS Security Hub with custom insights
AWS Systems Manager with compliance documents
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs) is the most appropriate solution for centrally managing and enforcing security policies across multiple accounts. SCPs can prevent the creation of public S3 buckets and restrict EC2 instance types at the organizational level, providing preventive controls that cannot be overridden by account administrators.

questions.question: A startup is building a new web application that expects rapid growth from 1,000 to 100,000 users within the first year. The application needs to be cost-effective initially but scale automatically as demand increases. Which architectural approach would be MOST suitable?
options: Use EC2 instances with Auto Scaling Groups, RDS with Multi-AZ, and CloudFront
Deploy on AWS Lambda with API Gateway, DynamoDB with on-demand billing, and CloudFront
Use ECS Fargate with Application Load Balancer, Aurora Serverless, and ElastiCache
Deploy on Elastic Beanstalk with RDS, use Reserved Instances for cost optimization
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most cost-effective and scalable solution for a startup: Lambda with API Gateway offers serverless scaling with pay-per-request pricing, DynamoDB with on-demand billing scales automatically without upfront costs, and CloudFront provides global content delivery. This architecture minimizes initial costs while automatically scaling to handle growth.

questions.question: A company's web application hosted on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer is experiencing slow response times during peak hours. CloudWatch metrics show high CPU utilization on the instances. Which immediate optimization would provide the MOST impact?
options: Increase the instance size to the next tier
Enable Auto Scaling based on CPU utilization
Add more instances manually
Implement CloudFront CDN
questions.explanation: Enabling Auto Scaling based on CPU utilization provides the most immediate and sustainable impact by automatically adding instances during peak demand and removing them when demand decreases, ensuring optimal performance while controlling costs.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate a simple web application from on-premises to AWS with minimal changes to the application code. The application currently runs on a single server with a MySQL database. Which migration approach would require the LEAST effort?
options: Rehost (lift-and-shift) using EC2 and RDS
Replatform to containers using ECS and Aurora
Refactor to serverless using Lambda and DynamoDB
Rebuild using cloud-native services
questions.explanation: Rehosting (lift-and-shift) using EC2 for the application and RDS for MySQL requires the least effort as it involves minimal changes to the existing application while providing the benefits of AWS infrastructure.

questions.question: A multinational corporation with subsidiaries in different countries needs to implement a data governance strategy that complies with GDPR, CCPA, and local data residency laws. The organization has 200+ AWS accounts across multiple regions and needs to ensure data doesn't cross certain geographical boundaries while maintaining operational efficiency. Which combination of services and strategies would BEST address these requirements?
options: Use AWS Organizations with SCPs to restrict cross-region data transfer, implement AWS Config rules for compliance monitoring, and use S3 bucket policies for data residency

Deploy AWS Control Tower with region-specific OUs, implement Resource Control Policies (RCPs) to restrict cross-region resource access, use AWS Macie for data classification, implement S3 Object Lock for data retention, and use AWS DataSync with region restrictions
Create separate AWS Organizations for each region, use cross-account IAM roles, implement AWS KMS with region-specific keys, and use CloudTrail for audit logging
Use AWS Organizations with declarative policies for data residency, implement AWS Security Hub for compliance monitoring, and use S3 Cross-Region Replication with restrictions
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive data governance solution: Control Tower with region-specific OUs enables geographical organization, RCPs restrict cross-region resource access to enforce data residency, Macie provides data classification for GDPR/CCPA compliance, S3 Object Lock ensures data retention requirements, and DataSync with region restrictions enables controlled data movement while maintaining compliance.

questions.question: A gaming company is building a new multiplayer online game that expects 500,000 concurrent players globally. The game requires real-time communication, player matchmaking, leaderboards, and in-game purchases. The architecture must support rapid scaling during game launches and minimize latency for players worldwide. Which architecture would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Use EC2 instances with Auto Scaling, RDS with read replicas, ElastiCache for leaderboards, and API Gateway for purchases
Deploy GameLift for game servers, DynamoDB Global Tables for player data, ElastiCache Global Datastore for leaderboards, API Gateway with Lambda for purchases, and CloudFront for content delivery
Use EKS clusters in multiple regions, Aurora Global Database, Redis Cluster mode, and Application Load Balancer
Implement ECS Fargate, DocumentDB with cross-region replication, MemoryDB for Redis, and AWS AppSync for real-time communication
questions.explanation: Option B provides the best gaming architecture: GameLift is purpose-built for multiplayer game servers with automatic scaling, DynamoDB Global Tables provide low-latency player data access globally, ElastiCache Global Datastore enables real-time leaderboards across regions, API Gateway with Lambda handles purchase transactions efficiently, and CloudFront reduces content delivery latency worldwide.

questions.question: A data analytics company's ETL pipeline is experiencing performance bottlenecks and high costs. The current architecture uses EC2 instances for data processing, S3 for storage, and RDS for metadata. The pipeline processes 10TB of data daily with varying workloads throughout the day. Processing times have increased from 2 hours to 8 hours, and costs have doubled. Which optimization strategy would provide the MOST significant improvement?
options: Scale up EC2 instances to larger sizes and add more RDS read replicas
Migrate to AWS Glue for ETL processing, use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for storage optimization, implement Amazon Athena for ad-hoc queries, and use AWS Glue Data Catalog for metadata management
Use EMR with Spot Instances, implement S3 lifecycle policies, and migrate metadata to DynamoDB
Implement Lambda functions for processing, use S3 Select for data filtering, and Aurora Serverless for metadata
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive optimization: AWS Glue offers serverless ETL with automatic scaling and cost optimization, S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes storage costs, Athena enables efficient querying without infrastructure management, and Glue Data Catalog provides managed metadata services. This combination addresses both performance and cost concerns while reducing operational overhead.

questions.question: A retail company is migrating their monolithic e-commerce application to AWS and wants to modernize it into microservices. The application handles product catalog, inventory management, order processing, and payment processing. They need to maintain data consistency across services and ensure zero downtime during the migration. Which modernization approach would be MOST effective?
options: Use the Strangler Fig pattern with API Gateway, gradually extract services to Lambda functions, implement EventBridge for service communication, and use RDS with cross-service transactions

Implement the Database-per-Service pattern with DynamoDB, use ECS for microservices, implement saga pattern for distributed transactions, use API Gateway for service mesh, and AWS App Mesh for service discovery
Deploy the entire application on EKS, use a single Aurora database, implement service mesh with Istio, and use Kubernetes deployments for gradual migration
Containerize the monolith first, then gradually extract services using ECS, implement event sourcing with Kinesis, and use Aurora Global Database for data consistency
questions.explanation: Option A provides the most effective modernization approach: The Strangler Fig pattern allows gradual migration without disrupting the existing system, API Gateway provides a unified interface during transition, Lambda functions offer serverless microservices, EventBridge enables loose coupling between services, and RDS can maintain ACID properties during the transition period before implementing distributed patterns.

questions.question: A government agency needs to implement a multi-account AWS environment with strict security and compliance requirements. They need separate accounts for different classification levels (Unclassified, Confidential, Secret), with no data flow between classification levels. The solution must support centralized identity management and audit logging while maintaining complete isolation between classification boundaries. Which architecture would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Use AWS Organizations with separate OUs for each classification, implement SCPs for isolation, use AWS SSO with SAML federation, and organization-wide CloudTrail

Create separate AWS Organizations for each classification level, implement AWS SSO in each organization, use separate identity providers, implement individual CloudTrail in each account, and use AWS Config for compliance monitoring

Use AWS Control Tower with classification-based OUs, implement both SCPs and RCPs for strict isolation, use AWS SSO with attribute-based access control, deploy separate CloudTrail organizations for each classification, and use AWS Security Hub with delegated administrators per classification
Deploy separate VPCs for each classification in a single account, use security groups for isolation, implement IAM policies for access control, and CloudWatch for monitoring
questions.explanation: Option C provides the most secure and compliant solution for government requirements: Control Tower with classification-based OUs provides proper organization, both SCPs and RCPs ensure strict isolation between classification levels, AWS SSO with ABAC enables fine-grained access control, separate CloudTrail organizations maintain audit isolation, and Security Hub with delegated administrators provides classification-specific security monitoring.

questions.question: A small business wants to build a simple website with a contact form that sends emails to the business owner. The website will have low traffic and the business wants to minimize ongoing maintenance. Which architecture would be MOST cost-effective and require the least maintenance?
options: Host on EC2 with a web server and use SES for email
Use S3 static website hosting with Lambda function for form processing and SES for email
Deploy on Elastic Beanstalk with RDS database
Use CloudFront with EC2 origin and RDS for data storage
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most cost-effective and low-maintenance solution: S3 static website hosting is very cost-effective for low traffic, Lambda function handles form processing without server management, and SES provides reliable email delivery. This serverless approach minimizes ongoing maintenance and costs.

questions.question: A media company's video streaming application is experiencing high bandwidth costs and slow loading times for users in different geographic regions. The current architecture uses EC2 instances in us-east-1 with S3 for video storage. Users are complaining about buffering issues, especially during peak hours. Which combination of optimizations would MOST effectively address these issues?
options: Add more EC2 instances and increase S3 storage class to Standard-IA
Implement CloudFront CDN with S3 as origin, use S3 Transfer Acceleration, and implement adaptive bitrate streaming with MediaConvert
Deploy EC2 instances in multiple regions and use Route 53 for traffic routing
Use Elastic Load Balancer with Auto Scaling and implement S3 Cross-Region Replication
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive solution for video streaming optimization: CloudFront CDN reduces bandwidth costs and improves global performance by caching content at edge locations, S3 Transfer Acceleration improves upload performance, and adaptive bitrate streaming with MediaConvert optimizes video delivery based on user connection quality, reducing buffering issues.

questions.question: A large enterprise is planning to migrate 500+ applications from multiple data centers to AWS over 18 months. The applications have varying architectures (mainframe, client-server, web applications), different database technologies (Oracle, SQL Server, DB2, MySQL), and complex interdependencies. The organization needs to maintain business continuity, minimize risk, and optimize costs during migration. Which comprehensive migration strategy would be MOST effective?
options: Use AWS Migration Hub for centralized tracking, implement a wave-based migration approach, use AWS Application Discovery Service for dependency mapping, deploy MGN for server migrations, use DMS for database migrations, and implement AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) methodology
Migrate all applications using lift-and-shift approach with AWS Server Migration Service, use AWS DataSync for data migration, and implement post-migration optimization
Use AWS Application Migration Service for all applications, implement blue-green deployment strategy, and use AWS Backup for data protection
Containerize all applications using AWS App2Container, migrate databases to Aurora, and use EKS for orchestration
questions.explanation: Option A provides the most comprehensive enterprise migration strategy: Migration Hub provides centralized visibility and tracking, wave-based approach manages complexity and risk, Application Discovery Service maps dependencies to prevent issues, MGN handles diverse server migrations with minimal downtime, DMS addresses various database technologies, and MAP methodology provides proven frameworks and potential funding for large-scale migrations.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure that all EC2 instances in their organization are launched with specific security groups and cannot be modified by individual account administrators. Which AWS service would be MOST appropriate for enforcing this requirement?
options: AWS Config with remediation actions
AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs)
AWS Security Hub with custom controls
AWS Systems Manager with compliance documents
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies (SCPs) is the most appropriate solution for enforcing security group requirements across the organization. SCPs can prevent the creation or modification of security groups that don't meet organizational standards, providing preventive controls that cannot be overridden by account administrators.

questions.question: A fintech startup is building a new real-time fraud detection system that must analyze millions of transactions per second, detect patterns using machine learning, and respond within 100 milliseconds. The system needs to handle varying transaction volumes, integrate with multiple payment processors, and maintain detailed audit logs for regulatory compliance. Which architecture would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Use API Gateway with Lambda functions, DynamoDB for storage, SageMaker for ML inference, and CloudWatch for logging

Deploy Kinesis Data Streams for ingestion, Kinesis Analytics for real-time processing, Lambda for ML inference, DynamoDB with DAX for low-latency access, and Kinesis Data Firehose for audit logging to S3
Use ECS with Auto Scaling, RDS with read replicas, SageMaker endpoints for ML, and CloudTrail for audit logging
Implement MSK for streaming, EMR for processing, Aurora for storage, and S3 for audit logs
questions.explanation: Option B provides the best real-time fraud detection architecture: Kinesis Data Streams handles high-volume transaction ingestion, Kinesis Analytics enables real-time stream processing, Lambda provides fast ML inference, DynamoDB with DAX offers sub-millisecond response times, and Kinesis Data Firehose ensures reliable audit logging to S3 for compliance requirements.

questions.question: A company's RDS MySQL database is experiencing high CPU utilization and slow query performance. The application primarily performs read operations with occasional writes. Which optimization would provide the MOST immediate improvement?
options: Upgrade to a larger RDS instance type
Add read replicas to distribute read traffic
Enable Multi-AZ deployment
Implement database connection pooling
questions.explanation: Adding read replicas would provide the most immediate improvement for a read-heavy workload by distributing read traffic away from the primary database instance, reducing CPU utilization and improving query performance without requiring application downtime.

questions.question: A company is migrating a legacy Java application that uses Oracle database to AWS. The application has tight coupling between application and database layers, uses stored procedures extensively, and requires minimal downtime during migration. The company wants to modernize the application architecture while maintaining compatibility. Which migration approach would be MOST suitable?
options: Migrate Oracle to RDS Oracle, containerize the Java application with ECS, and implement gradual refactoring
Use AWS DMS to migrate Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL, refactor stored procedures, and deploy application on Lambda
Migrate to Aurora MySQL, rewrite stored procedures, and use Elastic Beanstalk for application deployment
Keep Oracle on EC2, containerize application with EKS, and implement microservices architecture
questions.explanation: Option A provides the most suitable migration approach: Migrating to RDS Oracle maintains database compatibility and stored procedures, containerizing with ECS enables better resource utilization and deployment flexibility, and gradual refactoring allows modernization over time while minimizing risk and downtime during the initial migration.

questions.question: A consulting firm with multiple client projects needs to implement a multi-account strategy where each client has isolated environments but the firm needs centralized billing and security oversight. Each client project requires development, staging, and production environments with different access controls. Which organizational structure would BEST meet these requirements?
options: Create separate AWS Organizations for each client with consolidated billing
Use AWS Organizations with OU structure: Root > Clients > Projects > Environments, implement SCPs at appropriate levels, use AWS SSO for access management, and detailed cost allocation tags
Use a single AWS account with separate VPCs for each client and IAM policies for isolation
Create separate accounts for each client with cross-account IAM roles for management
questions.explanation: Option B provides the best organizational structure: The hierarchical OU structure (Root > Clients > Projects > Environments) enables proper isolation and governance, SCPs can be applied at different levels for appropriate security controls, AWS SSO provides centralized access management across all accounts, and detailed cost allocation tags enable accurate client billing while maintaining centralized oversight.

questions.question: A healthcare provider is building a new patient portal that must comply with HIPAA requirements. The portal needs to handle patient records, appointment scheduling, secure messaging, and integration with existing hospital systems. The solution must ensure data encryption, audit logging, and support for mobile applications. Which architecture would BEST address these requirements?
options: Use API Gateway with Lambda functions, RDS with encryption, CloudTrail for auditing, and Cognito for authentication

Deploy ALB with EC2 instances, Aurora with encryption at rest and in transit, AWS Config for compliance monitoring, CloudTrail for audit logging, Cognito User Pools for patient authentication, and VPC endpoints for secure communication
Use ECS Fargate, DynamoDB with encryption, CloudWatch for monitoring, and IAM for access control
Deploy on Elastic Beanstalk with RDS, use AWS KMS for encryption, and CloudFormation for infrastructure
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive HIPAA-compliant solution: ALB with EC2 provides reliable hosting, Aurora offers encryption at rest and in transit with high availability, AWS Config ensures continuous compliance monitoring, CloudTrail provides detailed audit logging, Cognito User Pools handles secure patient authentication, and VPC endpoints ensure secure communication with AWS services without internet exposure.

questions.question: A global e-commerce platform is experiencing inconsistent performance across different regions. The architecture uses CloudFront, ALB, EC2 Auto Scaling Groups, and RDS with read replicas. Users in Asia-Pacific report slow page loads and checkout failures during peak hours. CloudWatch metrics show high database connection counts and increased error rates in the ap-southeast-1 region. Which combination of optimizations would MOST effectively resolve these issues?
options: Add more EC2 instances in ap-southeast-1 and increase RDS instance size

Implement Aurora Global Database with regional clusters, deploy RDS Proxy in ap-southeast-1, add regional Auto Scaling Groups, implement ElastiCache Global Datastore for session management, and optimize CloudFront cache behaviors for dynamic content
Use Route 53 latency-based routing, add more read replicas, and implement connection pooling
Deploy additional CloudFront edge locations and increase ALB capacity
questions.explanation: Option B provides comprehensive regional optimization: Aurora Global Database enables low-latency reads in ap-southeast-1, RDS Proxy reduces connection overhead and improves database efficiency, regional Auto Scaling Groups provide local compute capacity, ElastiCache Global Datastore ensures consistent session management across regions, and optimized CloudFront cache behaviors improve dynamic content delivery performance.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate their file server from on-premises to AWS while maintaining the same file sharing protocols (SMB/NFS) for their existing applications. Which AWS service would be the MOST straightforward migration target?
options: Amazon S3 with S3 Transfer Acceleration
Amazon EFS (Elastic File System)
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is the most straightforward migration target as it provides fully managed Windows file systems with native SMB protocol support, maintaining compatibility with existing applications and user access patterns without requiring changes to client configurations.

questions.question: A large financial institution with 1000+ AWS accounts needs to implement a comprehensive security and compliance framework that supports multiple regulatory requirements (SOX, PCI-DSS, Basel III). The organization requires automated compliance monitoring, centralized security incident response, and the ability to quickly implement new security controls across all accounts. The solution must support different security postures for different business units while maintaining centralized oversight. Which architecture would BEST address these requirements?
options: Use AWS Organizations with SCPs, deploy AWS Config in each account, implement AWS Security Hub, and use AWS Systems Manager for patch management

Deploy AWS Control Tower with custom OUs for regulatory requirements, implement AWS Security Hub with custom security standards, use AWS Config with organization-wide conformance packs, deploy AWS GuardDuty with delegated administrator, implement AWS Audit Manager for compliance reporting, and use AWS Systems Manager for centralized patch management and incident response
Use AWS Organizations with basic structure, implement AWS CloudTrail in each account, deploy AWS Inspector for vulnerability assessment, and use AWS Trusted Advisor for recommendations
Create separate AWS Organizations for each regulatory requirement, implement individual security tools in each organization, and use cross-organization reporting
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive enterprise security and compliance framework: Control Tower with custom OUs enables regulatory-specific organization, Security Hub with custom standards supports multiple compliance frameworks, Config with organization-wide conformance packs ensures consistent compliance monitoring, GuardDuty with delegated administrator provides centralized threat detection, Audit Manager automates compliance reporting for multiple regulations, and Systems Manager enables centralized security operations and incident response.

questions.question: A startup is building a new mobile app that needs to store user profiles, handle user authentication, and send push notifications. The app expects moderate growth and the team wants to focus on application development rather than infrastructure management. Which combination of services would be MOST suitable?
options: EC2 with RDS, custom authentication system, and SNS for notifications
AWS Amplify with Cognito for authentication, DynamoDB for data storage, and Pinpoint for push notifications
ECS with Aurora, IAM for authentication, and SES for notifications
Lambda with RDS, custom JWT tokens, and CloudWatch for monitoring
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most suitable solution for a startup mobile app: AWS Amplify offers a complete development platform with minimal infrastructure management, Cognito provides managed user authentication and authorization, DynamoDB offers serverless data storage with automatic scaling, and Pinpoint provides comprehensive mobile engagement including push notifications.

questions.question: A SaaS application is experiencing high costs due to over-provisioned resources and inefficient resource utilization. The current architecture uses fixed-size EC2 instances, RDS instances running 24/7, and ElastiCache clusters that are underutilized during off-peak hours. Which cost optimization strategy would provide the MOST significant savings?
options: Purchase Reserved Instances for all resources and implement scheduled scaling

Implement Auto Scaling for EC2 instances, migrate to Aurora Serverless v2 for database workloads, use ElastiCache with scheduled scaling, purchase Savings Plans for consistent workloads, and implement AWS Cost Anomaly Detection for monitoring
Use Spot Instances for all workloads and implement basic monitoring
Migrate everything to Lambda functions and DynamoDB on-demand
questions.explanation: Option B provides the most comprehensive cost optimization: Auto Scaling ensures right-sizing of compute resources, Aurora Serverless v2 automatically scales database capacity based on demand, scheduled scaling for ElastiCache optimizes cache resources during off-peak hours, Savings Plans provide cost savings for predictable workloads, and Cost Anomaly Detection helps identify and prevent unexpected cost increases.
